answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 6 for each account already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The ember multiplier is published, charged in lantern, and copper lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, since the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 4810 identities would post 1936 proofs and burn roughly 61 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
